speaker: Unknown
en: If one is not reducing bureaucracy, there's no neutral ground.
zh: 如果有人不减少官僚主义，就没有中立地带。

speaker: Unknown
en: If one is not trying to improve things, it is going backwards.
zh: 如果有人不尝试改善事物，它就是在倒退。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to start in an unexpected place before we get into a bunch of other things.
zh: 我想从一个意想不到的地方开始，然后我们再进入一堆其他的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I want to talk about how keto changed your family's life.
zh: 但我想谈谈生酮如何改变了你家人的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is super interesting.
zh: 所以这超级有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had dabbled with keto maybe 10 or 12 years ago.
zh: 我大概在 10 到 12 年前偶尔尝试过生酮。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then this thing happened with my son where he got super bad bipolar probably eight to 10 years ago.
zh: 然后我儿子发生了一件事，他在大概 8 到 10 年前得了非常严重的双相情感障碍。

speaker: Unknown
en: We tried every medication.
zh: 我们尝试了每一种药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: We tried every solution to get him off medication.
zh: 我们尝试了每一种方案来让他停药。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here we were four or five or six years later, doctors had told him, you're going to be on five medications for the rest of your life.
zh: 于是就这样过了四五年或六年后，医生告诉他，你这辈子都要吃五种药了。

speaker: Unknown
en: He wasn't quite himself.
zh: 他不太像他自己了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lots of hospitalizations, all kind of stuff.
zh: 住院很多次，各种各样的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then out of the blue, someone I knew in the metabolic health community just said, hey, by the way, keto solved my bipolar.
zh: 然后出乎意料地，我在代谢健康社区认识的一个人就说，嘿，顺便说一下，生酮治好了我的双相情感障碍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can imagine after trying every resource in the world, right, just all these doctors and all of that, we said, let's give it a shot.
zh: 所以你可以想象，在尝试了世界上所有的资源之后，对吧，所有的医生和所有那些，我们说，让我们试一试吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we found a super smart keto doctor, super smart keto dietician.
zh: 所以我们找到了一个非常聪明的生酮医生，一个非常聪明的生酮营养师。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the fact that he said, I will try it.
zh: 他说愿意尝试，这让我感到……

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my gosh.
zh: 天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: What a relief.
zh: 真是解脱。

speaker: Unknown
en: Huge.
zh: 巨大的解脱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the next step, kind of three weeks in on the keto thing, was him saying, whoa, I feel a little different.
zh: 然后下一步，在做生酮这件事大概三周的时候，是他说的，哇，我感觉有点不一样了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And kind of picking up just a little bit more of him, still heavily medicated, but like the real him starting to poke through.
zh: 并且他稍微恢复了一点状态，虽然还在大量服药，但真正的他开始显露出来了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That must have been so hard on you and your wife as well.
zh: 这对你和你妻子来说肯定也非常艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So hard on us.
zh: 对我们来说太难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's really freaky is the number of families that it's that hard on.
zh: 真正令人毛骨悚然的是，有多少家庭正经历着那种艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we walk around the world and we see, you know, go to a football game and there's 60,000 people.
zh: 比如，我们在世界上行走，看到，你知道，去看一场橄榄球比赛，那里有 60,000 人。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's probably many people in that stadium going through that same thing.
zh: 在那个体育场里可能很多人正在经历同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was there ever a moment where you just felt like you were breaking?
zh: 有没有一个时刻你觉得自己快崩溃了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Luckily not.
zh: 幸运的是没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Either through some combination of, as you can imagine, here's this patient.
zh: 通过某种组合，正如你可以想象的那样，这里有一个病人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got to be there for him.
zh: 我们必须陪伴他。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's just like, okay.
zh: 所以就像是，好吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And luckily, I don't have what he has.
zh: 幸运的是，我没有他得的那个病。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do I, in a way, take care of myself so I can be there for him?
zh: 所以我该如何，在某种程度上，照顾好我自己以便我能陪伴他？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do you think about the relationship between mental health and our body, I guess, in that sense?
zh: 你如何看待心理健康和我们身体之间的关系，我想，在那个意义上？

speaker: Unknown
en: If I roll back the clock and think about my mind and how I thought about mental health 10 years ago, I use that as a template for how everyone without someone in their family must think about it.
zh: 如果我倒转时钟回想我的思想以及我 10 年前对心理健康的看法，我把那作为一个模板，来理解那些家里没有这样病人的人一定是怎么想的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just, oh, people go crazy.
zh: 就是，哦，人们发疯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, they're having a mental health thing.
zh: 哦，他们遇到了心理健康问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I never thought of it as a super physical thing.
zh: 我从来没把它当成一件非常生理的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because now I think of it as the same as a broken arm.
zh: 因为现在我认为它和手臂骨折一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just part of your body is physically not working.
zh: 就是你身体的一部分在生理上不运作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just happens to be your brain.
zh: 碰巧那是你的大脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: With this keto thing, I think I've developed a theory that in some cases, mental health things are very physical.
zh: 通过生酮这件事，我想我发展出了一个理论，在某些情况下，心理健康的事情是非常生理性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is your brain getting enough energy?
zh: 你的大脑获得足够的能量了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: The theory behind keto is that arguably we were eating some, you know, maybe more primeval foods up till 10,000 years ago.
zh: 生酮背后的理论是，可以说我们在 10,000 年前一直在吃一些，你知道，也许是更原始的食物。

speaker: Unknown
en: We hit the agricultural revolution.
zh: 我们遭遇了农业革命。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was wonderful in many ways.
zh: 这在许多方面是很棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our population flourished.
zh: 我们的人口繁荣了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in certain ways, we might not be fully adapted.
zh: 但在某些方面，我们可能还没有完全适应。

speaker: Unknown
en: There may be certain people who just are not fully adapted to that many carbs in their diet.
zh: 可能有些人只是没有完全适应饮食中那么多的碳水化合物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for my son, he may be one of those people.
zh: 所以对于我儿子来说，他可能是那种人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that launched a family foundation, I'd say, for the last four or five years doing research on this.
zh: 这启动了一个家族基金会,我想说,在过去四五年的时间里一直在做这方面的研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your current metabolic routine?
zh: 你目前的新陈代谢日常是怎样的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think I'm doing pretty well on not eating a lot of complex carbs that spike my glucose.
zh: 我确实认为我在不吃大量让葡萄糖飙升的复杂碳水化合物方面做得相当好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm wearing a CGM right now, so I have a little app on my phone and I can see my glucose level whenever I want to see it.
zh: 我现在佩戴着 CGM,所以我手机上有一个小应用程序,我可以随时查看我的葡萄糖水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you're not tracking your ketones?
zh: 但你没有追踪你的酮体?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not tracking my ketones, although I have in the past.
zh: 我没有追踪我的酮体,虽然我过去有追踪过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I kind of know.
zh: 所以我有点知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's going to spike me?
zh: 什么会让我飙升?

speaker: Unknown
en: But generally, I eat a fair amount of protein, a fair amount of fat, not too many carbs, and I don't eat any sugar.
zh: 但一般来说,我吃相当多的蛋白质,相当多的脂肪,不太多的碳水化合物,我不吃任何糖。

speaker: Unknown
en: I basically don't eat any starch, like anything that's going to give me a glucose spike.
zh: 我基本上不吃任何淀粉,比如任何会让我葡萄糖飙升的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does your metabolic state affect your decision making?
zh: 你的新陈代谢状态如何影响你的决策?

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think eating a lot of food or even a lot of carbs, we can all feel that kind of slow down, kind of hibernate, sleepy mode.
zh: 我确实认为吃很多食物甚至很多碳水化合物,我们都能感觉到那种减慢,那种休眠、困倦的模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in a more fasted state, you can feel that more alert, like I want to go do stuff kind of thing.
zh: 我认为在更多的禁食状态下,你可以感觉到更警觉,就像我想去做点什么的那种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I do think it's good to make decisions in that if you can tell the difference in that I want to go do stuff mode, I think those end up being longer term decisions.
zh: 我确实认为在这种状态下做决策是好的,如果你能分辨出那种我想去做点事的模式之间的区别,我认为那些最终会成为更长远的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can be decisions that, in a less optimistic mode, seem that that's impossible.
zh: 这些决策可以是那些,在不太乐观的模式下,看起来不可能的决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, that's so hard.
zh: 比如,这太难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do feel I have learned to tell when I'm in an on mood, when I'm in an off mood, when I'm a little more of an optimistic mode, which I think is general.
zh: 我确实感觉我已经学会了分辨我什么时候处于兴奋模式,什么时候处于关闭模式,什么时候处于更乐观的模式,我认为这是通用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do try to observe that from the outside in and say all big decisions make in the optimistic mode.
zh: 我确实尝试从外向内地观察这一点,并说所有重大决策都在乐观模式下做出。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do try to say, is the decision-making machinery in the optimal state?
zh: 所以我确实尝试说,决策机制处于最佳状态吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Outside of Roblox, how do you think about great products?
zh: 除了 Roblox,你如何思考伟大的产品?

speaker: Unknown
en: I like the notion of less is more.
zh: 我喜欢少即是多的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I like the notion of telling...
zh: 所以我喜欢告知的概念……

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone, it's very easy to add knobs and stuff.
zh: 每个人,添加旋钮之类的东西很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very hard to remove all of the knobs and sliders.
zh: 移除所有旋钮和滑块是非常困难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's fun when we think about products, like in a kitchen, for example, when we think about great products, I definitely would not like a dedicated appliance to cook hot dogs as opposed to...
zh: 当我们思考产品时很有趣,比如在厨房里,例如当我们思考伟大的产品时,我肯定不喜欢一个专门的设备来煮热狗,而不是……

speaker: Unknown
en: A beautiful knife and a beautiful frying pan.
zh: 一把漂亮的刀和一个漂亮的煎锅。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think I like simpler things of higher quality rather than complicated things.
zh: 所以我认为我喜欢更简单的高质量的东西,而不是复杂的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think of removing when it comes to the company?
zh: 当涉及到公司时,你如何思考做减法?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, there seems to be like sediment builds up inside the company and bureaucracy is the natural sort of like entropy of an organization.
zh: 我的意思是,似乎像沉积物在公司内部堆积,官僚主义是组织的熵的自然形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there has to be a counterforce almost to get rid of that.
zh: 然后必须有一个几乎相反的力量来摆脱它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do use the term destroy bureaucracy inside the company at times.
zh: 我们确实在公司内部使用"摧毁官僚主义"这个词。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say that if one is not reducing bureaucracy, there's no neutral ground.
zh: 我想说的是,如果一个人不减少官僚主义,就没有中立地带。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in a lot of situations where one thinks, we're pretty good, we're just going to let it be in this steady state, that's actually things are imploding in a way.
zh: 我认为在很多情况下,一个人认为,我们很好,我们就让它保持在这种稳定状态,实际上事情正在以一种方式内爆。

speaker: Unknown
en: If one is not trying to improve things,
zh: 如果一个人不试图改善事情,

speaker: Unknown
en: It is going backwards.
zh: 它就在倒退。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you give feedback to people?
zh: 你如何给人们反馈?

speaker: Unknown
en: What I have tried to do is move to more frequency, more in the moment, relaxed, not a big deal, rather than let's have a feedback session.
zh: 我试图做的是转向更多频率,更多在当下,轻松,不是什么大事,而不是让我们进行一次反馈会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: So trying to be in the moment.
zh: 所以试图在当下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, what do you think about that?
zh: 哦,你觉得那个怎么样?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think is much better than blocking or waiting or trying to organize it.
zh: 我认为比阻挡或等待或试图组织它要好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: How would you think that people receive that feedback?
zh: 你认为人们如何接受那种反馈?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the feedback is hyper tone-related.
zh: 我认为反馈与语调高度相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually think if delivered in a neutral positive tone where people can sense my blood pressure's not going up, where I'm just like, I got your back no matter what, it's all cool, even if the feedback's pretty harsh, it's like, whoa!
zh: 我实际上认为如果以中立积极的语调传达,人们可以感觉到我的血压没有升高,就像我不管怎样都支持你,这都很酷,即使反馈相当严厉,就像,哇!

speaker: Unknown
en: That was okay.
zh: 那还可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: So whereas I do feel if feedback is delivered aggressively or it's just like, oh, it's traumatic, I think that can actually influence it more than the feedback.
zh: 而我确实觉得如果反馈是激进传达的,或者就像,哦,这是创伤性的,我认为那实际上比反馈本身更能影响它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like the idea of tonal because so often we give, you know, when you distribute a workforce or people working from home, a lot of feedback is written over text or Slack or, and then you don't have that tone.
zh: 我喜欢语调这个概念,因为我们经常,你知道,当你分配劳动力或人们在家工作时,很多反馈是通过文本或 Slack 写的,然后你没有那种语调。

speaker: Unknown
en: ...or softness that goes with it.
zh: ……或者随之而来的柔和。

speaker: Unknown
en: I support that.
zh: 我支持那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, if I get riled up, like, don't touch text or email.
zh: 另外,如果我被激怒了,比如,不要碰文本或电子邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, just walk away.
zh: 比如,就走开。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you recognize it?
zh: 你认得它吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, yeah, just red alert.
zh: 哦，是的，正是红色警报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do not send that email.
zh: 不要发那封邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: To you or the one that you're about to send?
zh: 发给你还是你正要发的那封？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, just imagine writing an email where you're thinking, I'm so pissed off, it's gonna feel so good to send this email.
zh: 不，就想象写一封邮件，你在想，我很生气，发这封邮件会感觉这么爽。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't send that.
zh: 别发那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because then, like the next morning, you're like, oh my gosh, thank goodness I didn't send that.
zh: 因为那样，就像第二天早上，你会想，天哪，幸亏我没发那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can call this person.
zh: 我可以给这个人打电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I can have a lot more impact in delivering that same message without being all worked up about it.
zh: 我可以在传递同样信息时产生更大影响，而不用为此大动干戈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Plus also, what is one trying to optimize?
zh: 另外，一个人试图优化的是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: When someone's trying to send that email, I'm optimizing for myself.
zh: 当某人试图发送那封邮件时，我是在为自己优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas when the next morning comes around, you can say,
zh: 而当第二天早上到来时，你可以说，

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, actually, I should optimize for the learning and excitement of this employee.
zh: 嗯，实际上，我应该为这位员工的学习和热情而优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I like that a lot.
zh: 我非常喜欢这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think of it in terms of like outcome over ego.
zh: 我用结果胜过自我来思考它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just constantly trying to make it a better experience for the employee.
zh: 我们只是不断努力为员工提供更好的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who cares about me being pissed off?
zh: 谁在乎我是否生气？

speaker: Unknown
en: When you see people make mistakes, what are the patterns of mistakes that people make when it comes to seeing reality, ego, decision-making in that vein?
zh: 当你看到人们犯错时，在看待现实、自我、决策这方面，人们犯错的模式有哪些？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think there's a lot of mistakes.
zh: 我认为并没有很多错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the typical pattern is, hey, can we make this simpler?
zh: 我认为典型的模式是，嘿，我们能把这个做得更简单吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, can we look a couple years out and think about what's going to happen with that?
zh: 嘿，我们能展望几年后并想想那会发生什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: That looks a little short term.
zh: 那看起来有点短期。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, that looks a little complicated.
zh: 嘿，那看起来有点复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have two things doing the same thing.
zh: 你有两个东西在做同样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, can we take that from a appliance that heats up hot dogs?
zh: 嘿，我们能把它从一个加热热狗的电器吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: ...into two separate appliances, a pan and a knife that are both the best in the world.
zh: ...变成两个独立的电器，一个平底锅和一把刀，它们都是世界上最好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you spend a few beats and explain the principles of good decision making and good thinking as you see them?
zh: 你能花一点时间解释一下好的决策和好的思考的原则，正如你所看到的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There is something, I think, inside of an organization where for many decisions, it's actually more important just to let's identify the person who's going to make the decision and let them be somewhat free and creative to make the decision than in many cases a group decision or a confused decision or we're trying to do all of that.
zh: 我认为在组织内部有某种东西，对于许多决策，实际上更重要的是让我们识别出要做决策的人，并让他们在决策时有某种自由和创造力，而不是在许多情况下做一个集体决策或一个混乱的决策，或者我们试图做所有这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think you'll see more and more us at Roblox, it's just like, can we identify the decision maker?
zh: 所以我认为你会越来越多地看到我们在 Roblox 这样做，就像，我们能识别出决策者吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And having them have a little freedom to make their own decision I think is super powerful.
zh: 让他们有一点自由做出自己的决定，我认为这非常强大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Aside from systems thinking, what are some of the mental models that you use to think through problems?
zh: 除了系统思维，你使用哪些心智模型来思考问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one mental model that we've had in thinking through problems is kind of an irreverence in a way to the problem.
zh: 我认为我们在思考问题时有这样一个心智模型，某种程度是对问题的一种不敬。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, one of the decisions I think back to the early founding of Roblox, and I would call this a set of an irreverence is
zh: 你知道，回想 Roblox 早期创立时的一个决策，我会称之为一种不敬的集合，

speaker: Unknown
en: The very earliest version of Roblox had what we would call a classic Roblox character.
zh: 最早版本的 Roblox 有我们称之为经典的 Roblox 角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were saying, okay, we're building a user-generated gaming platform.
zh: 我们说，好的，我们正在构建一个用户生成游戏平台。

en: How do you deal with a situation where your instinct and the data disagree?
zh: 你如何处理你的直觉和数据不一致的情况？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting to think of the whole Roblox community and how smart and creative they are and how passionate they are.
zh: 考虑整个 Roblox 社区，思考他们是多么聪明和有创造力，以及他们是多么充满热情，这很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a really gentle line that needs to be worked on as we both drive the product forward as well as listen to that community.

speaker: Unknown
en: And that creates many conditions where our instincts are different than the community's vibe.
zh: 这创造了许多条件，让我们的直觉与社区的氛围变得不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: There have been situations where our instincts have been different.
zh: 已经有出现过我们的直觉不同的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: The community's been right.
zh: 社区是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's many other cases where instincts have been right and the community then follows along and says, that's an absolutely great idea.
zh: 还有很多其他情况，直觉是对的，然后社区随之跟上来说，那绝对是个好主意。

zh: 我们试图朝着正确的方向更快地做出决策。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can adjust.
zh: 我们可以调整。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for joining us.
zh: 谢谢你加入我们。

zh: 当事情没有按照你想要的方式发展时，在那些时刻，你的内心独白是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Interestingly, I think when we're running companies, we have all the evolutionary biology of being out there in the wilderness trying to survive and having battles and all of that.
zh: 有趣的是，我认为当我们经营公司时，我们要具备所有的进化生物学特征，就像我们在野外为了生存而战，经历战斗以及所有这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think CEOs can get that feeling like, oh my gosh, do I have enough firewood for the next three winters?
zh: 所以我认为 CEO 会有那种感觉，比如天哪，我为接下来三个冬天准备了足够的柴火吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, oh, it's not feeling too right.

zh: 对我来说，那一直是一种直觉性的早期思维活动。

zh: 好的是，它通常会带来策略上的改进，或者一点点……

zh: 你就像突然灵光一闪，就像哦，我们有了计划，我们确切地知道该做什么，我们要派四个人出去，他们都会有斧头，我们要储备三个月、三年的柴火，我们认为我们能在三周内完成

speaker: Unknown
en: Everything's great.
zh: 一切都很棒。

zh: 你会制造威胁作为一种激励或专注自己的方式吗？

zh: 我会想到迈克尔·乔丹为公牛队效力。

en: We are running right now a, I'm not going to say what the company looks like.

zh: 它不是一家现有的公司。

en: In my own mind, I have like, I'm imagining the company across the street that is like our, you know, could call it a threat.
zh: 在我自己的心目中，我有种，我在想象街对面的那家公司就像我们的，你知道，可以称之为威胁。

en: Yeah.

en: How do you do that?
zh: 你怎么做的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your process?
zh: 你的流程是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would just say my process, I would say typically my mistakes have come, I think, from being maybe overly logical and less intuitive.
zh: 我只想说我的流程，我想说我通常的错误都源于，我认为，可能过于逻辑化而不够直觉。

en: So trying to think of mistakes I have made have been typically where I've hung on to a concept too long.

zh: 每天有超过十亿人在玩手机游戏，专注，而不是滑动，没有信息流在争夺他们的注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Applovin puts your brand in front of the right customers and optimizes purely for your growth.
zh: Applovin 将您的品牌展示在合适的客户面前，并纯粹为您的增长进行优化。

en: I mean, it might be.

zh: 我认为我学到的是，我们需要对这个虚拟世界里的所有所有人给予极大的尊重。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's surprising how much people can attach to their digital identity.
zh: 我认为人们对他们的数字身份的依恋程度之深是令人惊讶的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it has to be very carefully respected.
zh: 我的意思是，这必须非常小心地予以尊重。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is real stuff, right?
zh: 这是真实的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: There are real emotions happening, real interactions happening.
zh: 那里有真实的情感在发生，真实的互动在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think I've also learned that I feel it's still very, very early in this.
zh: 而且我觉得我也学到了，我感觉这仍然处于非常非常早期的阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say more about attaching to your virtual identity.
zh: 多说说关于对虚拟身份的依恋。

en: Once again, this is an area that I love the Roblox community on, and I think they're very sensitive to this, in that we're migrating all of our avatars to a position where, rather than just being a monolithic block,

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the migration of this process, the Roblox community has just been absolute sticklers for perfection in the migration.
zh: 但在这个过程的迁移中，Roblox 社区一直是迁移过程中完美的绝对吹毛求疵者。

zh: 我认为他们是对的。

en: Super thoughtful.

en: Knock on wood, we've made a lot of cash in our history, like a lot of positive free cash flow.
zh: 祈求好运，我们在历史上赚了很多现金，就像很多正向的自由现金流。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the decisions we make have come from not necessarily capital allocation, but what are we trying to do?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 机会的大局是什么，以及我们正试图从哪里增长？

en: I would say we've refined that many times throughout our history.
zh: 我想说的是，我们在历史上已经多次完善了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go deeper on that.
zh: 再深入谈谈那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we just thought that was, oh, that's huge.
zh: 我们只是认为那是，哦，那是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like Club Penguin, like they've got, you know, X many people.
zh: 就像 Club Penguin，就像他们有，你知道，很多人。

en: We like what they're doing.

en: We started with arguably a much bigger, deeper technical foundation.
zh: 我们开始时的基础可以说要大得多、深厚得多。

en: I would say, though, along the way, we've refined our aspiration and what we're trying to do.
zh: 我想说的是，不过，在这个过程中，我们已经完善了我们的愿望和我们要做的事情。

zh: 两年前，我们谈论让全球 10% 的游戏来到我们的平台上。

en: I think you'll continue to hear us kind of expand our ambition.
zh: 我想你会继续听到我们要拓展雄心。

en: That's amazing.

en: That's incredible.

en: It's incredible, and at the same time, it actually seems like it's exciting to me because there's a lot of room beyond three or four percent.
zh: 这确实不可思议，同时，这对我来说似乎很令人兴奋，因为在百分之三四之外还有很多空间。

en: What about incentives for people?

en: What have you gotten right and gotten wrong over the years?
zh: 这些年来你们做对了什么，做错了什么？

en: We thought that would be an amazing incentive and we thought that would give us amazing amounts of content.

speaker: Unknown
en: That did prove to be really true.

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a hobby for everyone.
zh: 这对每个人来说都是一个爱好。

speaker: Unknown

en: So I think going after, say, our vision is 10% of the gaming market, that's a pretty good focus.
zh: 所以我认为，比如说，我们的愿景是占据游戏市场的 10%，这是一个很好的专注点。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people understand it, but I think that constantly should be reevaluated a bit as we think about where we're going in the future.
zh: 很多人都能理解，但我认为，随着我们思考未来的发展方向，这一点应该不断进行重新评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you use AI internally to help make decisions or help expand your context window in the company?
zh: 你们在内部使用 AI 来帮助做决策或帮助扩大公司的上下文窗口吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say we have all kinds of AI.
zh: 我想说的是我们有各种各样的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a bunch of internal systems that we have built.
zh: 我们建立了一系列内部系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, we have a thing called the Roblox operating system that we use for tracking the work in the company more and more, helping people see how they fit into the organization.
zh: 所以，你知道，我们有一个叫作 Roblox 操作系统的东西，我们越来越多地用它来跟踪公司的工作，帮助人们看到他们如何融入组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are all like MCP enabled, so anyone can take their AI system and run it on top of those.
zh: 这些都是启用了 MCP 的，所以任何人都可以使用他们的 AI 系统并在这些系统之上运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a way, we think of all of our Roblox systems as things that either people or AI can look at and run things against.
zh: 在某种程度上，我们将我们所有的 Roblox 系统视为人员或 AI 可以查看并运行操作的对象。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have all kinds of people building custom little things that are looking at the work tracker or doing some things.
zh: 所以我们有各种各样的人在构建自定义的小东西，用于查看工作跟踪器或做一些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people auto-generate our one-on-one discussion topics.
zh: 有些人会自动生成我们要进行的一对一讨论的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would say, yeah.
zh: 所以我想说，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to get into talking about
zh: 我想开始谈论

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of the policy that's coming out of governments all around the world in terms of age bands, how do you think, without commenting maybe on whether they should or should not exist, who do you think should implement those?
zh: 世界各地政府出台的许多关于年龄段的政策，你认为，在不评论它们是否应该存在的情况下，你认为应该由谁来实施这些政策？

speaker: Unknown
en: Should those be at the company level specifically, or should they be at a platform level like Apple?
zh: 这些应该具体在公司层面实施，还是应该在像 Apple 这样的平台层面实施？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, when I talk to senators in the United States, I say, please, how can we help you take a look at what we've done on our own?
zh: 我是说，当我和美国的参议员交谈时，我说，拜托，我们要如何帮助你们查看我们自己做了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Without any laws requiring it, we're now using AI to check the age of every single person on our platform.
zh: 在没有任何法律要求的情况下，我们现在正在使用 AI 来检查我们平台上每个人的年龄。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've open sourced our voice safety filter.
zh: 我们开源了我们的语音安全过滤器。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've done this, this, and this.
zh: 我们做了这个，这个，还有这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do say, look at what private industry can do.
zh: 所以我确实会说，看看私人行业能做到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one thing.
zh: 所以这是一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then of course, I think there has to be a lot of
zh: 然后当然，我认为必须有很多

speaker: Unknown
en: Thought and caution.
zh: 思考和谨慎。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think universally legislators I've met with, they do have a balancing act.
zh: 我认为我见过的立法者普遍都有一种平衡行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are trying to enact great legislation, but they're trying not to have the tragedy of good intentions.
zh: 他们试图制定伟大的立法，但他们试图避免“好意带来的悲剧”。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're trying not to craft laws that's just like, oh my gosh, I wish we wouldn't have done that.
zh: 他们试图避免制定这样的法律，那就是，天哪，我希望我们没有那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, one could say, for example,
zh: 你知道，人们可能会说，例如，

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, on a mobile phone, whoever makes the mobile phone should check the age of everyone on the mobile phone.
zh: 嗯，在手机上，制造手机的人应该检查手机上每个人的年龄。

speaker: Unknown
en: We said we're not waiting for that.
zh: 我们说我们不会等待那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're going to do it ourselves in a way.
zh: 我们在某种程度上会自己动手做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But do you think that that is a better solution from an industry point of view
zh: 但是你认为从行业的角度来看，这是一个更好的解决方案吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or do you think it's better for, you're not waiting, that's great, but do you think it's more elegant to have it at a device level or at an individual company and you're responsible for that?
zh: 还是认为，你并没有等待，这很好，但你认为把它放在设备层面，还是放在单个公司层面并由你负责会更优雅？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is what makes it so tricky in that I would say both, in that knowing what we do, given that we're doing age check for all of our users, for comms, for example,
zh: 这就是为什么这件事如此棘手，因为我会说两者都是，鉴于我们所做的，考虑到我们正在为我们所有的用户、例如在通信方面进行年龄检查，

speaker: Unknown
en: We know, for example, a lot of parents don't have the time to configure their device, or a lot of parents just say, yeah, take my iPad and go do that.
zh: 我们知道，例如，很多父母没有时间配置他们的设备，或者很多父母只是说，是的，拿走我的 iPad 去做那个吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if that iPad is configured, for example, as a parent and it's handed off to a kid, that can be a little tricky.
zh: 所以如果那个 iPad 被配置为父母模式然后交给了孩子，这可能会有点棘手。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would say even when devices maybe have an age in them, we'll still keep doing our own thing.
zh: 所以我会说，即使设备里可能有年龄信息，我们仍然会继续做我们自己的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that's had a cost on you.
zh: 但这对你来说是有代价的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was listening to your last earnings call this morning, and it slowed down growth.
zh: 我今天早上听了你上次的财报电话会议，增长放缓了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say the opportunity to build a global platform that has more and more people playing together, which is amazing, and all around the world, not just, quote, over 13, but of all ages, I mean, this is foundational to our growth.
zh: 我想说的是，打造一个全球性平台的机会，让越来越多的人一起游玩，这很棒，而且在全世界范围内，不仅仅是，引用一下，超过 13 岁，而是所有年龄段，我的意思是，这是我们增长的基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we're very optimistic.
zh: 就像，我们非常乐观。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think where I was going with that is you're able to take a longer view in part because you're a majority shareholder.
zh: 我想我想表达的是，你之所以能够采取更长远的视角，部分原因是因为你是大股东。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're the founder.
zh: 你是创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You carry a lot of weight in that.
zh: 你在那里面有很大的分量。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can make these decisions.
zh: 你可以做这些决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not every company is going to feel that they can take an immediate short-term pain for longer-term gain.
zh: 不是每家公司都会觉得他们可以为了长期利益而承受眼前的短期痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I would say this is, once again, where our aspirations are.
zh: 是的，我想说这再一次反映了我们的愿景所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: We think digital play is just amazing.
zh: 我们认为数字游戏很神奇。

speaker: Unknown
en: We shared we're in the 3% to 4% of the world right now.
zh: 我们分享了我们在全球目前处于 3% 到 4% 的水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagining what the future is going to be for the types of interactions we're going to have, it's pretty amazing.
zh: 想象一下我们将要拥有的互动类型的未来会是什么样子，这是非常令人惊叹的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do just feel the work we've done, safety, civility, platform-wide, is foundational for platforms like this.
zh: 所以我确实觉得我们在安全、文明、全平台方面所做的工作，对于这样的平台来说是基础性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you close your eyes, I want you to tell me what Roblox looks like in five years from now.
zh: 如果你闭上眼睛，我想告诉我五年后的 Roblox 是什么样子的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll share a couple examples.
zh: 我会分享几个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: One, we shared the other side of that, which is the technology we're building for Roblox Reality.
zh: 第一，我们分享了另一面，也就是我们正在为 Roblox Reality 构建的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's surprising that it's actually hard to imagine...
zh: 令人惊讶的是，实际上很难想象...

speaker: Unknown
en: What a photorealistic multiplayer game would feel like.
zh: 一款照片写实的多人游戏会有什么感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, we're not used to it.
zh: 就像，我们还不习惯它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're used to looking at gaming footage and saying, that is an amazing game.
zh: 我们习惯看着游戏画面说，那是一款神奇的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: That looks so good.
zh: 看起来太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think when we look at it, we say, but that is a game, by the way.
zh: 但我确实认为当我们看它的时候，我们会说，但那是游戏，顺便说一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is not, that's not like Bourne Identity, you know?
zh: 那不是，那不像《谍影重重》，你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And whereas if we ran Bourne Identity on a 2K screen,
zh: 而如果我们在 2K 屏幕上运行《谍影重重》，

speaker: Unknown
en: That looks different than that.
zh: 那看起来和那不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do think there's going to be a future world where we have all the aspects of the multiplayer gaming interesting, but it feels like that.
zh: 所以我确实认为会有一个未来的世界，我们在其中拥有多人游戏的所有有趣方面，但它给人的感觉就像那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's going to be pretty mind-blowing.
zh: 我认为那将会非常震撼。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be a little bit like going from black and white to color, or going from 512 to 2K.
zh: 这将有点像从黑白到彩色，或者从 512 到 2K。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, people don't quite realize how big that can be.
zh: 就像，人们还没有完全意识到那会有多大。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's one aspect of it.
zh: 所以我认为那是其中的一个方面。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's another aspect where the notion of you make the game is really going to come full circle because games are much more complicated than code.
zh: 我认为还有另一个方面，也就是你制作游戏这个概念将真正实现完整闭环，因为游戏比代码复杂得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have images and assets and they have environments and they have stories and they have all of that.
zh: 它们有图像和资产，它们有环境，它们有故事，它们有所有这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: But getting to the point where you or I
zh: 但达到你或我

speaker: Unknown
en: Make a beautiful thing, share it with our family, play it just by talking about it I think is going to come true as well.
zh: 制作出美丽的东西，与我们的家人分享，仅仅通过谈论它就能玩到它，我认为这也将会成为现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: This episode is brought to you by Accenture.
zh: 本集由埃森哲为您带来。

speaker: Unknown
en: When your advertising operations fall out of sync, everything else follows.
zh: 当你的广告运营步调不一致时，其他一切也会随之脱节。

speaker: Unknown
en: Spotify and Accenture are working together to reinvent the rhythm of ad sales using automation, analytics, and smarter workflows to simplify campaign delivery and access better data across the business.
zh: Spotify 和埃森哲正在合作，利用自动化、分析和更智能的工作流程重新定义广告销售的节奏，以简化活动交付并在整个业务范围内获取更好的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: The result?
zh: 结果呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Less time spent on operations, more time connecting brands with the moments and fandoms that matter most.
zh: 在运营上花费的时间更少，有更多时间将品牌与最重要的时刻和粉丝群体联系起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more at Accenture.com slash Spotify.
zh: 了解更多信息请访问 Accenture.com slash Spotify。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that that's credible.
zh: 我认为那是可信的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think will be the second and third order consequences of that?
zh: 你认为由此产生的第二和第三层后果会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the positive thing to think about is actually the fun parts around connection and digital play will, in a way, become very... they're already quite meaningful.
zh: 我认为要考虑的积极的事情实际上是，关于连接和数字游戏的有趣部分，在某种程度上会变得非常... 它们已经相当有意义了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the consequences will be...
zh: 我认为后果将会是...

speaker: Unknown
en: More fluidity in digital play.
zh: 数字游戏更加流动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: The feeling that it's not me as a user and them as a creator.
zh: 这种感觉，即我作为用户而他们作为创作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: The notion, it'll almost be like in the old days, only 1% of us were oil painters documenting the king's portraiture.
zh: 这个概念，它几乎就像在旧时候，只有 1% 的我们是描绘国王肖像的油画家。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas now, I think we all feel like we're oil painters.
zh: 而现在，我想我们都感觉像是油画家。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have our phone, we have digital image tools, and we're all kind of feeling like we're part of it.
zh: 我们有我们的手机，我们有数字图像工具，我们都有一种感觉像是参与了其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a way, rather than a digital technology like reducing the job market for oil painters, it's probably increased the job market.
zh: 在某种程度上，与其说像数字技术那样减少了对油画家的工作需求，它可能反而增加了工作市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot more people doing digital imagery.
zh: 现在做数字图像的人多多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm actually thinking the same thing will happen for gaming and that both the hardcore creator market and all of us will be more involved in the creation of immersive experiences.
zh: 我其实认为游戏领域也会发生同样的事情，无论是硬核创作者市场还是我们所有人，都会更多地参与到沉浸式体验的创作中。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was your reaction to watching Ready Player One?
zh: 你看《头号玩家》时是什么反应？

speaker: Unknown
en: Ready Player One, the book I loved, the movie V1 I loved, but I do like less intrusive, you know, far out VR.
zh: 《头号玩家》这本书我很喜欢，电影 V1 我也很喜欢，但我确实喜欢那种侵入性较小的，你知道的，那种更遥远的 VR。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd say like Black Mirror, when they do VR, like you just put a little white dot on you and it like takes over your eyes and your body and all of that.
zh: 就比如说《黑镜》，当他们做 VR 时，就像你身上放了一个小白点，它就接管了你的眼睛和你的身体以及所有这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's less intrusive.
zh: 它的侵入性较小。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's probably more where it's gonna go, probably, than just goggles and stuff like that.
zh: 我认为这大概可能才是它的发展方向，大概，而不是仅仅是护目镜之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Huge fan of Ready Player One, but I think there's a wide range of, like, technical coverage of how this is gonna work.
zh: 我是《头号玩家》的超级粉丝，但我认为这有一系列广泛的，比如说，关于这一切如何运作的技术覆盖范围。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a stickler, I would say, on sci-fi movies.
zh: 我是个挑剔的人，我会说，关于科幻电影。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, the more real...
zh: 就是越真实……

speaker: Unknown
en: And the less comedy or glitchy or whatever, the more I like it.
zh: 越少喜剧性或故障感或者什么都没有，我就越喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's really hard to find sci-fi movies that are just trying to be real.
zh: 我觉得真的很难找到那些只是试图变得真实的科幻电影。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to get this right, so I'm going to read this, but my 16-year-old submitted a question for you.
zh: 我想把这件事弄对，所以我来读一下这个，但我 16 岁的孩子为你提交了一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: My 16 year old.
zh: 我 16 岁的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you were starting out at 16 today with no money, no contacts, no network of people that you could rely on, how would you spend the next five years to maximize your chances of building a company that matters?
zh: 如果你今天从 16 岁开始，没有钱，没有人脉，没有你可以依赖的人际网络，你会如何度过接下来的五年，以最大化你建立一家重要的公司的机会？

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my gosh.
zh: 天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would, well, I'll tell them what worked for me is that was the last thing on my mind when I was 16.
zh: 我会，好吧，我会告诉他们，对我有用的方法是，那是我 16 岁时脑子里最没想到的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I was into, in a way, hang out with people I liked.
zh: 就像我某种程度上喜欢，和我喜欢的人混在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was into what naturally I was good at and interested in, whether it was building model rockets or go-karts.
zh: 我热衷于我天生擅长和感兴趣的事情，无论是制造模型火箭还是微型赛车。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if one is 16 and actually that's what you're into, there is a notion to, as one goes through the normal course of life, you're going to go to high school, you're going to maybe go to college.
zh: 我认为如果你 16 岁并且实际上那就是你的兴趣所在，有一种概念是，当你经历正常的生活过程时，你要去上高中，你可能会去上大学。

speaker: Unknown
en: In parallel, can that be your fun little hobby in a way?
zh: 与此同时，那能不能成为你的一种有趣的小爱好？

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you warm up on that in an authentic way?
zh: 你能不能以一种真实的方式在那上面热身？

speaker: Unknown
en: We always end these interviews with the same question, which is, what is success for you?
zh: 我们总是以同样的问题结束这些采访，那就是，对你来说什么是成功？

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel every day I'm already feeling very successful.
zh: 我觉得每一天我都已经感觉很成功了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I feel like I'm in a way- What goes into that feeling?
zh: 所以我觉得我在某种程度上——这种感觉源于什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel waking up every day just saying I'm so fortunate.
zh: 我觉得每天醒来只是说我太幸运了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually feel that way.
zh: 所以我确实有那种感觉。
